docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Welcome to The Shattered Pale, a diverse and expansive world shaped by grand deities of a forgotten era. After a ruinous and divisive war, the Celestials, Dragons, and Primordials were banished away, incapable of fully returning to their creations.

Now, in the distant future, the people of the world are still recovering from their absence. Divine power channeled by the devout trickles through the imperfect veil, arcanists wrestle with the chaos of the magical weave, and fractured alliances and rising factions race to uncover ancient artifacts or otherwise strengthen their influence.

docs.title: Myth and Legend
docs.text: • Superstitions, folktales, and rumors are commonplace. While many are pure fiction, shaped by the great storytellers of past generations, some may be worth believing in.

docs.title: Exploration and Adventure
docs.text: • The war-torn world is full of abandoned ruins, forgotten relics, and bountiful caches. Many trailblazers and opportunists alike find the allure of adventure, and profit, too great to ignore.

docs.title: Dangerous and Rare Magic
docs.text: • For a time, powerful gods used magic to shape the world and its people, before passing it down to their students. Today, magic practitioners are rare and their spells often unstable.

docs.title: Political Intrigue
docs.text: • In the dominions of court and council or crime and corruption, only those strong enough can thrive. Play your cards right and your choices can shift alliances, shape nations, and end (or begin) wars.

docs.title: Resting
docs.text:
• Short rests require the party to take at least 8 hours of downtime, usually at the end of a day, during which they can perform only light activity. If this downtime is interrupted by more than a half hour of heavy activity (fighting, spellcasting, traveling, etc), the character gains no benefit from the rest.

  • Long rests require the party to take at least 48 hours of downtime in a safe area, during which they can perform normal downtime activities such as crafting, carousing, researching, gambling, shopping, light training, etc.

docs.title: Death Saves
docs.text:
• If a player needs to roll a Death Save, it is to be done in private -- neither the DM nor the other players should see or know the outcome.

  • Whenever you are making Death Saves and either Stabilize or heal above 0 HP, you receive 1 level of Exhaustion. You cannot exceed 5 levels of Exhaustion in this way.

  • Last Stand - Once per Long Rest, you can choose to use the Last Stand ability before rolling a Death Save. Doing so allows you to take an Action and move up to half your speed (in either order). During the Last Stand, you cannot regain any hit points or receive any temporary hit points. After the Last Stand ends, you automatically receive 2 failed Death Saves and must proceed to roll another Death Save before ending your turn.

docs.title: Combat
docs.text:
• Tactical Initiative Shift - After initiative is rolled, the party may collectively decide whether half of the group (rounded down) will relinquish their rolled initiative scores. These characters immediately move to act directly before or after a chosen ally in the turn order. The characters choosing to move can only move down in initiative. This decision must be made before any creature takes its first turn in combat.

  • Desperate Casting - Once per short rest, a character with the Spellcasting feature may strain their magical reserves to regain a spell slot. As a bonus action, they recover one expended spell slot of their choice, up to 4th level, and immediately gain a number of levels of exhaustion equal to the level of the recovered spell. This ability cannot restore spell slots beyond the highest level the character can normally cast.

docs.title: Character Creation
docs.text: • At level 1, choose one skill in which you have proficiency. You gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it.

docs.title: Skill Challenges
docs.text:
Skill Challenges measure a group’s ability to work together to execute a complex plan, survive a hazardous environment, or overcome a multi-stage obstacle.

To complete a Skill Challenge, the party must accumulate a target number of successes before reaching a specific threshold of failures (for example, 5 successes before 3 failures to escape a collapsing two-story dungeon, or 7 successes before 3 failures for a larger three-story dungeon). Players act in turns, with each turn allowing a player to make a check or expend a resource toward the party's goal.

  • Rules of Engagement:

    • Proficiency & Non-Proficient Checks: Players are encouraged to rely on their heroic archetypes by utilizing skills in which they have proficiency. A player may attempt a check using a skill in which they lack proficiency, but doing so significantly increases the Difficulty Class (DC) of the check.

    • Per-Player Skill Limits: An individual character cannot use the same skill more than once during a single Skill Challenge. However, different characters may use the same skill (for example, two different players may both attempt an Athletics check during separate turns).

    • Expending Resources: A player may sacrifice a spell slot or a limited-use feature (such as Channel Divinity or a Superiority Die) to contribute to the challenge. Depending on the resource used and its relevance to the situation, the DM determines whether the effort grants Advantage on the check or bypasses the check entirely to award an automatic success.

    • Consequences of Failure: Reaching the failure threshold does not always result in a Total Party Wipe or complete failure. Instead, it often introduces significant setbacks, lingering complications, lost time/resources, or immediate new hazards that the party must now face.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Endaros is a nation that controls a large portion of Ardona, primarily in the south. It was originally settled by Humans and remains predominantly Human in population. However, other species also reside there—most notably, the Genasi.

While Endaros maintains peaceful relations with its southern neighbors in Soland, trade and travel across Athera's Strait remains rare. Endaran Humans tend to harbor lingering resentment toward the Aasimar due to the banishment that happened in generations past. Tensions are notably higher with the Human nation of Bellatora, whose northern provinces seceded from Endaros following a civil war. The border between them remains unstable and ever-shifting.

docs.title: History
docs.text: Endaros is the first nation settled by Humans and one of two nations that controls Ardona. After a cohort of Aasimar were severed from their divine ancestry and stripped of their access to magic, they were banished from Soland and sent north towards Ardona. Their original settlement in Southern Ardona grew into what is now Endaros.

docs.title: Culture
docs.text: Information about the culture, traditions, and daily life in the country.

docs.title: Government Structure
docs.text: Details about the government, its structure, and political climate.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Ardona is a small continent in the Northern Hemisphere, curving westward as it stretches north. Its southern edge meets the oceanic waters of Athera’s Strait, a natural divide from the continent of Soland. The terrain shifts from coastal cliffs and windswept lowlands to craggy highlands and deep glens, growing harsher the farther north one travels.

Though remote, Ardona is not stagnant. Trade routes hug the coast, and strategic passes in the narrowing north are fiercely contested.

docs.title: Climate
docs.text:
Ardona’s climate is a study in severity and contrast, defined by its tapering geography and relentless northern winds. The southern reaches, closest to Athera’s Strait, experience cool maritime conditions—frequent rain, biting gusts, and short summers that allow for hardy crops from rocky soil. Fog rolls in from the strait, cloaking the coastlines, while inland valleys remain damp year-round.

As one travels northward, the land rises and the climate grows increasingly harsh and unforgiving. Winters are long and brutal, with snowdrifts swallowing roads and frost overstaying its welcome. The highlands are home to violent storms, sudden temperature drops, and a near-constant wind that howls through passes and ravines. Even in summer, warmth is fleeting.

This climate has shaped a culture of resilience and austerity. Architecture favors thick stone walls and turf roofs; clothing is layered, woolen, and built for durability. The people of Ardona know the weather not as a condition, but as a constant presence and force to be respected. It is said that the wind remembers the betrayal that brought them here, and that the cold is the land’s way of keeping them humble.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
The Humans of Ardona are the descendants of Aasimar, cast down and stripped of their celestial birthright. Banished to the cold reaches of the north, they first settled in the southern lowlands. Over generations, they pushed northward, driven by ambition and resentment, taming the native fauna, and conquering scattered Genasi clans who once roamed the highlands. These Primordial-born peoples were subdued and forcibly assimilated—now their customs survive only in fragments, buried beneath the dominant Human culture.

But unity did not last. A brutal civil war split the exiled into two nations: the south, proud of its ancestral settlements and wary of change, and the north, forged in conquest and hardened by frontier life. Though they share blood, the two nations now stand divided by ideology, memory, and the lingering question of who truly carries the legacy of the fallen divine. The Genasi, though silenced, reside beneath the surface—neither fully erased nor entirely accepted.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: To the southeast of Soland, across warm equatorial currents and shifting trade winds, lies Sa Zortao. It is dominated by dense jungles, where vines hang like curtains and the air hums with unseen life. Rivers carve through the forest's undergrowth like veins of silver, feeding sprawling wetlands. Beyond the rainforests, adventurous explorers can hike across volcanic cliffs or through grasslands nestled in mountain valleys.

docs.title: Climate
docs.text:
Sa Zortao’s climate is a symphony of heat and moisture, shaped by its position in the southern tropics. The continent’s jungles flourish with humidity, where rain falls in thick sheets. Monsoon cycles bring floods, saturate the canopy, and summon blooms so vivid they seem otherworldly.

Highlands and volcanic plateaus offer cooler air, while savannas and dry forests stretch across the rain-shadowed interior, marked by seasonal fires and golden grasses. Coastal regions are warm and stormy, shaped by ocean currents and salt-laden winds. Across Sa Zortao, the climate is studied, woven into ritual calendars and agricultural cycles.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
The Dragonborn of Sa Zortao descend from ancient bloodlines said to align with the sky-serpents of myth. They dwell in cities and villages carved into cliffs and jungle clearings, with stepped ziggurats, bustling plazas, and celestial observatories.

Festivals mark solstices and eclipses, when drums echo through the jungle and sacred fires burn for days.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: South of the cold winds of Ardona lies Soland, a geographically varied continent of sunlit coasts, rolling grasslands, and dense woodlands. A vast inland sea cuts through its eastern half, bringing salty air and lucrative trade to the surrounding regions. Along its shores, maritime cities adorned with monuments to the gods thrive. Farther inland, beyond rocky peaks and winding valleys, stretch ancient and watchful woods.

docs.title: Climate
docs.text:
Shaped by its central sea and diverse topography, Soland offers many geographical settings. Around the inland sea and coastal regions, the air is warm and fragrant, with long, golden summers and rainy winters. Sea breezes carry warmth and moisture into the cities and smaller valleys, creating a sense of fertility and ease.

The central plateau features drier grasslands and deserts and is the home of nomadic groups, deserters, and those drawn to the frontier.

To the north, the terrain cools, giving way to temperate forests and misty hills. Here, the seasons shift more sharply. Autumns blaze with color, winters bring frost and silence, and spring arrives with a rush of green and birdsong. Rain is frequent but gentle, feeding moss-covered glades and verdant woodlands.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
Throughout Soland, especially along the coasts, are collections of city-states and nations. Although primarily made-up of Aasimar and Elves, many [races](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home) and cultures are present. However, the largest sovereign state is a theocracy led by Aasimar seers, where divine order rules and old traditions are held sacred.

Scattered deeper into the continent lie old Elven kingdoms, each with its own customs, courts, and tangled alliances. Some are serene and scholarly, others wild and warlike, but all are deeply tied to the land, its seasons, and its memory.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Far to the east of Soland and Sa Zortao, and standing as a sister‑continent to Khor, lies Tsugash, a land known for its beauty and bloodshed. It features emerald forests, mist-laden coasts, and old and snowcapped peaks. Despite the natural splendor, the people of Tsugash live in a state of tension. Clans, city-states, and wandering war bands clash over old grudges and diverging beliefs. The continent’s story is one of breathtaking abundance paired with unending struggle.

docs.title: Climate
docs.text: Though some regions lean temperate, all four seasons arrive in full force across Tsugash. Winters sweep down from the northern ranges, coating the land in snow and turning mountain passes into treacherous corridors. Spring bursts forth with wildflowers and rushing rivers that carve through fertile valleys. Summers are warm and bright, drawing laborers into the open fields. Autumn sees that the forests turn red and gold before the first snows return.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Tsugash is home to many peoples, but [Orcs](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home) and [Goliaths](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home) form its cultural backbone. Their societies are as varied as the terrain they inhabit. Ancient Orcish clans trace their bloodlines back centuries, guarding traditions of honor, ancestor worship, and martial discipline. [Goliaths](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home) are a relatively new inhabitant, immigrating to Tsugash after the war, and causing some discontent in the process. Over time, Orcish clans have lost power as sovereign democracies form, but some refuse to lose the power they obtained generations ago.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Aestios came to Raasha from distant galaxies, eventually forming an alliance with the resident titans, the Dwasti and Anazuatl. The three pantheons agreed to share stewardship over the planet and its resources.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Before the Aestios arrived, Raasha was in a state of chaos. The Dwasti and Anazuatl had spent millennia on the planet, cycling between periods of peace and war. At the time, the planet's only inhabitants were non-sentient lifeforms and the gods themselves.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Nobody knows exactly how Raasha was created, nor do they know who its first residents were — both of which remain subjects of great debate. Scholars fear the true answers have been lost or were never accurately recorded in the first place. Despite the wide variety of faiths, theories, and stories found across Raasha today, most assume that the planet's first residents were either the Dwasti or the Anazuatl.

It is well known that these two groups shared the planet for millennia. Possessing the might and immortality of gods, yet lacking the ability to create life, these supreme beings were trapped in a cycle: neither could fully destroy the other, and they did not know what to do with their gifts.

That changed when the Aestios arrived. Announcing themselves as celestial travelers who navigated by the constellations, they brought new possibilities to the realm. Though the natives of Raasha were initially skeptical, an alliance was forged after an unknown span of time. The Aestios offered a trade: they would teach the other gods how to create life, provided that the planet and its resources were shared equally among the three pantheons and their future offspring. The deal was struck, and for a time, the gods worked together in harmony.

GM Secret

Very few know the hidden truth: the Aestios were renegades who fled their nomadic, star-traveling clan to find a world where they could seed new existence. Though creating life was strictly forbidden among their kind, they believed it was their sacred duty to pass on their celestial gifts and lineage. Unbeknownst to them, however, their escape did not go unnoticed—and they were followed.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The War for Raasha was a planet-spanning conflict that shattered the ancient age of divine harmony. Triggered by a covert betrayal among the gods, the decades-long war devastated mortal civilizations, scarred the realm's natural landscapes, and permanently severed the deities from walking directly alongside their creations.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Following the pact between the pantheons, three elder races were brought into existence: the Aasimar of the Aestios, the Dragonborn of the Anazuatl, and the Genasi of the Dwasti. For an era, these lineages flourished under the direct guidance of their creators, establishing grand civilizations before giving rise to subsequent mortal races.

Unbeknownst to the realm, however, an enigmatic faction of celestial pursuers—the former clan of the Aestios—had tracked the renegades to Raasha. Watching from the shadows, these pursuers secretly infiltrated both mortal societies and the native pantheons, subtly sowing discord, jealousy, and suspicion.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The secret orchestration culminated in a catastrophic betrayal, turning factions within the native pantheons against the Aestios and plunging the entire planet into war. Spanning decades, the conflict saw the rise and fall of countless mortal alliances, the destruction of ancient cities, and the divine empowerment or arcane ascension of extraordinary individuals who claimed godhood amidst the chaos.

As the catastrophic power of the gods irreversibly scarred the land and fractured the bonds between races, a desperate coalition of mortals took drastic action. Prioritizing the planet's survival over divine loyalty, this group enacted a grand ritual that sealed all pantheons away from Raasha behind an impenetrable cosmic veil.

In the post-war era, the physical presence of the gods on Raasha came to an end. While their power still bleeds through the veil—allowing clerics, warlocks, and scholars to tap into divine magic and ancient secrets—the deities can no longer walk among mortals, leaving a scarred world to rebuild in their shadow.

docs.title: Age of Cosmos
docs.text:
1. Group of Aestios (celestials) abscond from their community.

    1. The celestials come from a nomadic group of star-powered gods, the Aestios. They created constellations as ways of traversing the universe.

    2. Using certain types of magic was forbidden, like using it to create new life or end conflicts -- neutrality was law.

  2. Celestials come to Raasha, which is inhabited by ancients -- The Anazuatl (dragons) and Dwasti (primordials).

    1. Dragons were the masters of arcane magic, primordials of primal magic, and celestials of divine magic.

  3. A peace pact was signed by the three groups. In exchange for a residency on the planet, the celestials would teach the dragons and primordials how to create new life.

  4. The newly formed trinity of godlike beings create their first kind -- the Deva.

docs.title: Aestios
docs.text: The Aestios are a benevolent pantheon of star-faring celestials who navigated the cosmos by charting new constellations before arriving on Raasha. Revered across the realm for their deep wisdom, they fundamentally reshaped history by bestowing the secret art of life-creation upon the world's native gods.

docs.title: Anazuatl
docs.text: The Anazuatl are a majestic pantheon of draconic, feathered serpent gods celebrated as the supreme masters of arcane magic, time, and space. Despite their incredible cosmic mastery, their legacy is forever shadowed by a catastrophic ancient civil war fought between their two most powerful deities.

docs.title: Dwasti
docs.text: The Dwasti are the primordial titans of Raasha, embodying the raw elemental forces and physical majesty of the world itself. Manifesting in wildly distinct physical forms tied to their natural domains, these ancient deities presided over the planet's oceans, mountains, and cataclysms long before mortal history began.

docs.title: Ziratu
docs.text: The Ziratu are a secretive, taboo pantheon revered and feared as the silent architects of the Great War. Operating from the shadows in humanoid form, these cosmic pursuers infiltrated mortal societies, inadvertently spawning the original Tiefling bloodlines before sealing their own fate behind the Veil.

docs.title: Species Traits
docs.text:
• Languages: Celestial
  • Lifespan: Adulthood - 40+, Life Expectancy - 200
  • Common Names: Thaliorus, Elystria, Astrelius, Lurimaros

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Aasimar are angelic mortals infused with a divine connection to the stars and moons beyond Raasha, recognized by many as one of the three Elder Races. Though most cannot consciously wield their celestial gifts, all Aasimar experience prescient dreams that echo their cosmic heritage. Aasimar often look to the night's sky for guidance, divining with constellations and trying to connect with their creators.

Most hail from eastern Soland, their ancestral homeland, but they can be found throughout the civilized world. They are often perceived as condescending and aloof, even though they view themselves as an enlightened people. Relaxed, steady, and fearless in the face of uncertainty.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Aasimar commonly bear features reminiscent of the cosmos: radiant eyes, metallic skin, or moonlit veins. In stature, they are generally comparable to other mortal peoples of Raasha. Each year an Aasimar lives, a faint star-shaped mark appears somewhere on their body. As these soft, dull lights accumulate with age, they form a personal tattoo-like constellation. Many spend their lives seeking a meaning hidden within their sign.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Dawnborn - Blessed by rising light, their cosmic features carry warm, gentle hues. They’re known for optimistic attitudes and a drive to explore and grow.

  • Duskborn - Shaped by twilight’s contrast, their dimmer features glow in cool tones. They tend to be reflective, patient, and drawn to a life of introspection and contemplation.

  • Lifespan: Adulthood - 20+, Life Expectancy - 100
  • Common Names: Tzamak, Ozmel, Mixaleth, Zyotlan

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
As their name implies, Dragonborn are the humanoid descendants of the feathered serpent gods of old. Being one of the three Elder Races, Dragonborn appear as bipedal versions of their draconic ancestors, carrying both the physical presence and elemental power of the ancient dragons. Their ability to exhale elemental energy makes them natural arcanists, but they are just as well known for their legendary warriors as for their sorcerers.

Most Dragonborn hail from Sa Zortao, their jungle homeland, though some clans have migrated to distant lands for reasons unknown to outsiders. Their historic cities rise from canopies and mountainsides with towering temples and bold monuments, each one a testament to their pride and long memory. Dragonborn are passionate people, famous for their vibrant festivals and equally famous for their quick tempers.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Dragonborn are tall, muscular, and covered in scales, with horned heads and vibrant feathers. Their facial structure and general appearance is that of a dragon in humanoid form. The color of their scales reveals the element they were born to wield and exhale. Their lifespan is average among the peoples of Raasha and shorter than their Elder Race kin, but they live with a fierce intensity, as if every day might be their last.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Chromatic - Descended from the radiant serpent‑god [Tec‑Natz‑Tum](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home), the Prism Serpent, they embody the full spectrum of elemental power. Their scales range in color, hinting at the element they can exhale, and their temperaments tend to be bold, expressive, and unpredictable.

  • Metallic - Born of the platinum serpent [Zatl’ka](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home), they embody discipline, strength, and refined martial skill. Their scales gleam like worked metal, and their elemental breath is controlled and precise, but they are best known for their unmatched warriors.

GM Secret

Gem - Descended from a mysterious cosmic serpent whose domain is space and time, they are calm, introspective, and perceptive. Their scales shimmer with crystalline hues, and their breath carries echoes of distant stars or temporal distortion.

docs.title: Species Traits
docs.text:
• Languages: Dwarven
  • Lifespan: Adulthood - 40+, Life Expectancy - 300

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Dwarves are a hardy and intelligent people, renowned for their engineering skill and remarkable craftsmanship. Most Dwarven societies are self-sufficient and insulated, with the people departing from their cities mainly to trade.

Hailing from Khor, a land of harsh deserts and deep canyons, the Dwarves have carved out a bountiful life for themselves by inventing technology that helps them shape the land around them. Their reputation for being cold or selfish comes from their focus on their own kin and allies, valuing others based on usefulness and proven commitment. However, their destructive inventions have also given them a long‑standing stereotype as warmongers, though most see their work simply as tools for survival.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Dwarves are short and stocky, and live longer lives than most. Their ever-growing hair is usually neatly maintained and often decorated with small baubles that show status or wealth. They are sturdy in build, practical in action, and carry an unshakable confidence.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Mountain Dwarves - Born in the high peaks and deep canyon fortresses of Khor, they are steady, guarded, and slow to trust, but unmatched in stonework and engineering. Mountain Dwarves usually have fair skin and light eyes, shaped by generations spent underground and away from the sun.

  • Dune Dwarves - Shaped by the harsh dunes and shifting heat of Khor’s lowlands, they are resourceful, quick‑thinking, and skilled at crafting tools that survive extreme conditions. Dune Dwarves often have dark skin and hair, but their eyes are strikingly colorful.

docs.title: Species Traits
docs.text:
• Languages: Elvish
  • Lifespan: Adulthood - 40+, Life Expectancy - 400
  • Common Names: Eldureth, Iruvelon, Syndos, Otarielle

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Elves are magical beings born of materialized spirits. When creatures on Raasha die, traces of their memories and experiences linger in the spiritual world. Ages ago, a powerful sorceress learned to harness this essence and reform it into new life. It remains a sacred ritual still practiced today. When an Elf is born naturally instead, they inherit fragments of memories directly from their family line.

Connected to the spirit world, Elves possess an innate magic that lets them sense and shape its currents. Their collective memories give them a deep appreciation for knowledge and a reverence for tradition. Like Dwarves, most Elves rarely stray far from their homelands. They often speak in a thoughtful, measured tone, and their spiritual awareness lends them a serene, calming presence.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Elves are slightly smaller than average humanoids due to their slender frames. While they resemble Humans in many ways, they have pointed ears, sharp features, and an ageless appearance. Remarkably agile and light on their feet, their movements carry an effortless grace.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Dreamwalkers - When they dream, Dreamwalker Elves sometimes live through the memories of spirits. They perceive these dreams in real time, with a single rest feeling like days or weeks spent living another's long-lost life. This constant influx of historical perspectives leaves them deeply introspective, possessing an uncanny wisdom. Sometimes called Night Elves or Drow, they have skin in grayish hues of blue or purple.

  • Fateweavers - By studying the flow of the spirit world, Fateweaver Elves read the collective mass of Raasha's memories to divine what is to come. Viewing history as a repeating tapestry, they sense the spiritual momentum of past choices to anticipate danger before it strikes. Commonly called High Elves, they are typically taller than other Elves and possess a calculating foresight.

  • Spiritspeakers - Attuned to forgotten voices, Spiritspeaker Elves act as direct bridges between the living world and wandering spirits. Through painted runes or carved totems, they can allow the dead to speak through them or perform rituals to commune with nature spirits. Commonly known as Wood Elves due to their northern forest kingdoms, they possess warm, earthy hair and skin tones.

docs.title: Species Traits
docs.text:
• Languages: Primordial
  • Lifespan: Adulthood - 30+, Life Expectancy - 150
  • Common Names: Varash, Raithu, Minali, Suryak

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Genasi are the first descendants of the Primordial titans, the godlike beings who shaped the world long before written history. As one of the three Elder Races, they once stood alongside the Aasimar and Dragonborn in unity. Their three subraces, Flora, Fauna, and Terrana, each carry the spark of a different titan, giving them a natural tie to the lands and living forces their ancestors watched over.

Since the war, the Genasi have suffered more than most. Their cities fell, their numbers dwindled, and many were forced into a nomadic life. Today, most Genasi travel in small tribes, moving with the seasons and relying on tight‑knit communities for survival. Only a few settlements remain fully under their control, and even those are scattered across distant regions. Though they once held vast territories, Genasi are now found all over the world, often far from the lands their subraces once called home.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Genasi generally resemble [Humans](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home) in shape and appearance but carry clear signs of their Primordial heritage. Flora Genasi may show hints of growth or bloom, Fauna Genasi carry animal‑like vitality or features, and Terrana Genasi show the strength and stillness of stone and soil. All subraces have a wide range of skin and eye colors, from blue to yellow to grey, usually marking their titan heritage.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Flora Genasi - Shaped by the Primordial of growth and bloom. They are calm, patient, and steady, with small signs of plant life appearing in their hair, skin, or scent.

  • Fauna Genasi - Descended from the Primordial of living creatures. They are instinctive, energetic, and adaptable, often showing faint animal traits like sharper senses or subtle markings.

  • Terrana Genasi - Born from the Primordial of all non‑living matter. They are steady, resilient, and slow to bend. Their features may hint at stone, metal, sand, or even water‑smooth skin and tide‑cool blood, marking them as children of the earth in all its forms.

GM Secret

docs.title: Species Traits

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Goliaths were the second race shaped by the old Primordial gods, created after the Genasi but with a very different purpose. Where the Genasi embodied the raw forces of the natural world, Goliaths were forged to endure those forces. Though they can wield elemental power, their true gift lies in surviving it, channeling it, and refusing to break beneath it. This distinction has long fueled a rivalry with the Dragonborn, a race they once warred against, whose own elemental abilities and imposing stature often invite comparison neither race appreciates.

Goliath culture is built on challenge, blunt honesty, and the pursuit of personal glory and exceptionalism. It is common—expected, even—for young Goliaths to leave their clans and seek a name for themselves. Long ago, their people were subjugated by the Giants, forced into labor and hardship until they eventually won their freedom. Because of this history, Goliaths still speak the Giant tongue, though many use it reluctantly. They are famously competitive, measuring themselves and others through feats of strength, endurance, or courage, and while they respect their ancient connection to the Primordials, they strongly dislike being compared to their Genasi kin.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Goliaths are the largest of all humanoid races, towering over others with broad frames and powerful builds. Their skin ranges through shades of gray and brown, and their inky black eyes often carry speckles or thin veins of color that stand out against their features. Natural markings run across their skin in patterns reminiscent of tattoos, typically indicating the clan or family they come from.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Volcanic - Volcanic Goliaths are acclimated to eruption zones, enduring blistering heat, acidic steam, and toxic volcanic gases that would kill most others.

  • Typhonic - Typhonic Goliaths are shaped by storm fronts that feature freezing blizzards, sky‑splitting lightning, and thunderous shockwaves.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Humans are the stubborn descendants of the Aasimar who turned against their gods during the War and were stripped of their divine birthright. Banished from Soland to the harsh northern continent of Ardona as punishment, they have quietly grown in isolation while maintaining tight-knit communities that have never forgotten their fallen past.

Though most remain in their northern homeland, adventurous or outcast Humans can be found across Raasha working as sailors, mercenaries, and laborers. Tempered by generations in Ardona’s unforgiving wilderness, Humans are notoriously persistent, driven, and quick to hold a grudge—yet deeply reliant on the strength of their own communities.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Humans bear a striking resemblance to their Aasimar ancestors, though they lack their cosmic longevity and star-touched features. Their skin, hair, and eye tones are more grounded and muted, and they tend to possess slightly broader, stockier builds than average Aasimar, while remaining comparable in stature to the other mortal peoples of Raasha.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
Humans have no subraces.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Orcish folktales describe a time when their ancestors weren't people at all, but fearsome monsters known as Oni who roamed throughout Tsugash in violent rages. These traditional stories passed down for generations say that one by one, Oni awakened to clarity and consciousness. From this mysterious surge of enlightenment came the first Orcs, who chose to pursue a path of discipline, tempering their ancestral power with purpose and honor.

A history of defending their homeland from would-be conquerors has shaped a culture among Tsugash Orcs where mastery of the blade became essential for survival. Today, Orc clans have slowly descended into civil war, out of differing political opinions, old grudges, or pride. Yet Orc folklore warns that endless bloodshed risks awakening the old nature of the Oni they once were, a superstition taken seriously by many clans. Because of this, a growing number of Orcs strive for peace, believing that honor is found in temperance rather than victory.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Orcs are tall and broad‑framed, with tusks, pointed ears, and pronounced brow and jaw lines. Their skin ranges from grey to muted greens and blues, and their eyes are often bright warm colors like orange or yellow. Although many on Raasha think of Orcs as brutish because of their appearance, their introspective and refined natures show a people who value restraint, reflection, and the mastery of themselves.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
Orcs have no subraces.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Saurians are often mistaken for Dragonborn because of their scaled skin and shared Draconic tongue, but there is no known relation between the two peoples. Their true origin remains a mystery, with only scattered stories hinting at where they first emerged. Outsiders sometimes view Saurians as uncivilized or savage, yet most live peaceful lives in close‑knit communities that value nature, kinship, and simplicity over grandeur. Lizardfolk and Tortles primarily inhabit The Emerald Reach, a warm archipelago between Sa Zortao and Soland, while Kobolds are found mostly throughout the deserts and mountains of Khor. While they originally hailed from Sa Zortao, wars with the Dragonborn led to a large diaspora.

Saurian society is shaped by cooperation, practical skill, and a deep respect for the natural world. Their settlements are modest but well‑adapted to their environments, built from local materials and arranged around communal spaces where food, labor, and responsibility are shared. While each subrace (and each community) has its own customs and ways of life, all Saurians value self‑sufficiency and the bonds they share with their kin. Their communities may appear primitive to outsiders, but they are resilient, resourceful, and deeply rooted in the lands they inhabit.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Saurians vary widely in appearance, but all share scaled skin, animalistic athleticism and senses, and features shaped by their environments. Together, they form a diverse but unified people whose forms reflect the places they call home.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Lizardfolk - Patient hunters and swift swimmers with crocodile‑like bodies and eel‑shaped faces, known for their keen senses and strong connection to the wetlands and jungles.

  • Tortle - Broad‑framed, slow‑moving people who resemble bipedal tortoises, valued for their calmness, sturdy shells, and steady presence within their island communities.

  • Kobold - Small, quick, and clever desert and mountain dwellers who rely on tight‑knit packs, sharp instincts, and resourcefulness to survive in the harsh lands of Khor. They often live in subterranean communities, and they have quickly adapted to the cold dark.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Tieflings are mortals imbued with the covert, cosmic essence of the Ziratu—the secretive celestial pursuers who infiltrated Raasha before [The War](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home). While the world often misinterprets their striking physical features as demonic, their true lineage traces back to cosmic hunters who walked hidden among early humanoids. Though the Ziratu have long since been sealed behind the Veil, Tieflings inherit an innate instinct for uncovering secrets, reading subtle intentions, and navigating shadow.

Most hail from the sun-cured coastal trade hubs and grand oasis city-states of southern Soland, across the sea from the Aasimar realms. While often viewed with suspicion or prejudice due to their ancestors' role in [The Great War](The%20Shattered%20Pale%20(Wiki%20Home), Tieflings tend to be pragmatists and charming. Resilient and self-reliant, they value cunning, loyalty to chosen kin, and surviving in a world that fears their origins.

docs.title: Physical Traits
docs.text: Tieflings bear striking markers of their ancestors' hidden nature, characterized by sharp features, solid-colored obsidian or opalescent eyes, and prominent horns that sweep from the brow or temple. Skin tones range from rich terracotta and sun-bleached copper to deep indigo or ash. Some Tieflings are born with prehensile tails, though just as many possess none. As a Tiefling ages, their horns grow in size and complexity—developing intricate ridges, spirals, or heavy crests over decades that serve as a physical record of their longevity and maturity.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
Tieflings have no subraces.
